# AWS Database Migration Service

Store replication subnet groups, instances, endpoints and tasks as records only, with no data migration.

**Status: implemented subset.** Operation selection does not imply complete input or behavior parity.

| Contract | Current implementation |
| --- | --- |
| Service ID | `databasemigrationservice` |
| Signing name | `dms` |
| Wire protocol | AWS JSON 1.1 |
| API version | `2016-01-01` |
| Scope | Account and region |
| Execution | Records only |
| Selected operations | 22 of 119 in the pinned model |

## Implemented behavior

See the [implemented feature catalogue](catalogue.md#aws-database-migration-service) for this service's capabilities.

## Limitations and future work

- Records only, no data migration: no replication compute, connectivity tests, table statistics, logs, CDC checkpoints, network allocation or real completion is claimed.
- Certificates, event subscriptions, account attributes, serverless replication configurations and other DMS APIs are not implemented.
- Instance modifications apply to metadata synchronously, including deferred requests; maintenance windows are metadata, not scheduled. Engine versions and classes are checked syntactically rather than against a regional catalog.
- A replication subnet group must be explicitly supplied when creating an instance. No IP addresses or KMS keys are provisioned.
- Endpoint settings are metadata only; nested authentication fields, certificate references, exact settings replacement and DMS Transfer settings are rejected. Top-level and nested passwords and other Smithy-sensitive settings are accepted and discarded.
- Task CDC start/stop positions and timestamps, task data, custom resource identifiers and Kerberos settings are unsupported. Table mappings are checked for structural validity, not evaluated.
- Transitions advance only for the returned Describe page; inventory and tag reads do not advance them. Full-load completion is simulated and moves no data.
- No CloudFormation resource provider.

These gaps describe current boundaries and possible follow-up slices. The [roadmap](../roadmap/index.md)
separates proposed work from registered functionality; there are no promised release dates.

The table is generated from the profile and pinned Smithy model. Routes show REST bindings or the standard
JSON/Query endpoint. RPC v2 CBOR uses its service/operation route, as described in
[protocol handling](../architecture/request-flow.md). Supported members are selected separately in the
